Messages.Author: Magnus Giritzlehner
Messages.Body:
OK... A Toreador vs. blue blood(ventrue)
the Toreador plays a "Riposte"
the blue blood playes a "Majesty"
Question: Does the "Riposte" do the 1(2) damage to the blue blood?

Magnus Giritzlehner

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
a94m...@student.his.se (Magnus Giritzlehner) writes:



I'd guess "yes", since the damage from riposte is somehow (not yet
explained) granted immunity from the termination of the strike
resolution phase (as caused by Riposte). It must, therefore, be
immune to further terminations of the strike resolution phase.

Of course, the "damage unpreventable" text on Riposte combined with
the lack of a strike resolution phase in which to inflict damage
should lead a casual reader to determine that Riposte's damage is
done after the "Combat Ends" effect - that is, after the combat is
ended. If this were the official case, the resolution of the
dilemma presented above would be trivially obvious. However, the
Rules Team prefers the inconsistency of dealing damage in a phase
which no longer exists. This will lead to some strange situations.

That is how it used to be when S:CE resolved the moment it was played
(since the acting minion announced his strike first).

But now, the two S:CE resolve at the same time (during strike
resolution). They are the same effect, so neither has precedence.

The section (page 30 in the V:tES rulebook) is a reworking
of the rules attempting to clarify the earlier mis-rule from
Jyhad - that the blocker doesn't announce a strike if the
acting minion plays a S:CE. It is badly worded enough to
yield "the acting minion's S:CE is superior to the blcoker's
S:CE", but this should obviously not be the case.

S:CE resolves beofre any other type of strike, but precedence
is never given to the acting minion's strike resolution, only
to the acting minion's strike declaration.

Suppose both minions announce "strike: steal 2 blood" as their
strikes. Does the acting minion's Strike: steal blood resolve prior to
or simultaneously with the blocking minion's Strike: steal blood?

TOM?
Is it the intention of pg. 30 in the V:tES rulebook to make the
acting minion's strike resolve first (or can we have a little
errata to remedy the loophole)?



Messages.Author: Zaphod Beeblebrox
Messages.Body:
Rory (refp...@best.com) wrote:

: Well if the acting minion plays a combat ends strike then the Reacting
: minion cannot play a strike card for effect but only to cycle thier
: hand should they so desire.
: Of course this is a pretty specific issue and I may have forgotten a
: ruling here.
: I know there was one on this issue but don't remember what it was
: exactly.
: Rory
: The Ref at refp...@best.com

This is not entirely true. For example, a blocking minion on
combat could play superior majesty in response to a similar
strike by the acting minion in order to untap. A better way to
look at it is that since the strike resolution phase is
skipped, _most_ strikes available to the blocking minion would
be ineffective and useful only to cycle cards. Riposte would
be an exception similar to superior magesty, since its damage
is dealt in some mysterious strike resolution phase which comes
before all the ones which were cancelled by the strike: combat
ends.
